items.title: Define a complete routine validation identity and shared trusted metadata lineage contract
items.context: Extract the exact-head/trusted-story-metadata-descendant lineage core from done-prepare validation reuse, and bind routine validation evidence to command specs and digests, configured/fallback/validate-file source, full/profile/focus, and verification policy/coverage inputs. Legacy evidence without identity is never reusable.

happy.desc: Given each supported routine validation source, when the effective plan is resolved, the stored validation identity deterministically covers source kind, normalized ordered command specs and command or entrypoint digests, full/focus/profile, plus verification policy and coverage inputs; changing none reproduces the same identity. WHY: reuse is sound only when PASS evidence names every input that can alter what validation means or executes.

Given exact-head and trusted story-metadata-descendant histories, when routine validation and DONE reuse classify lineage, both consumers return the same shared lineage result and reason. WHY: one lineage contract prevents routine validation from becoming weaker than the existing DONE trust boundary.

edge.desc: Given configured commands, fallback discovery, and validate-file execution that happen to resolve to similar text, when identities are calculated, source-specific inputs and executable digests remain represented and stable optional defaults canonicalize consistently. WHY: visually similar plans can have different trust and execution semantics.

Given a prior identity, when command order, cwd, env, timeout, config, entrypoint content, full/focus/profile, or verification policy/coverage inputs change one at a time, the identity changes; unrelated story metadata alone does not change it. WHY: every behavior-affecting delta must invalidate reuse without metadata churn causing false invalidation.

adversarial.desc: Given legacy PASS evidence with no complete validation identity, or evidence with missing, malformed, unknown-version, or partially forged identity fields, the reuse classifier rejects it and requires execution. WHY: compatibility must fail closed to real validation, never upgrade incomplete historical evidence to PASS.

Given a descendant HEAD containing any non-trusted commit among metadata commits, renamed paths, or a code/material change disguised by a trusted-looking message, shared lineage rejects metadata-descendant reuse. WHY: commit prose or endpoint hashes alone must not launder implementation changes into trusted metadata lineage.

items.title: Short-circuit fresh routine PASS validation under the execution lock
items.context: Before executeValidationPlan, read prior PASS evidence and reuse only when coverage is complete, materialHash/storyFilesHash and validation identity match, lineage is exact or trusted metadata-only, the tree is clean, and HEAD remains stable across the decision. Any read/hash/lineage/TOCTOU uncertainty falls back to real execution, never to PASS.

items.title: Expose an auditable executed-versus-reused disposition without metadata churn
items.context: Return and persist enough structured identity for future decisions while a reused result remains byte-stable: do not rewrite test-evidence, do not auto-commit metadata, and report precise refusal reasons for changed commands, config, entrypoint, focus/full/profile, policy, dirty tree, malformed evidence, untrusted lineage, or TOCTOU drift.

items.title: Prove safe reuse and fail-closed fallback across every validation source
items.context: Add table-driven coverage for configured commands, fallback discovery, validate-file branches, exact-head and metadata-descendant reuse, dirty tree, legacy/malformed evidence, command/config/entrypoint/full/profile/policy changes, incomplete coverage, failed prior evidence, and HEAD changes during the locked decision. Include a regression reproducing B-19ca: commands already PASS, only verificationEvidence refreshes, next validation reuses instead of running 45 commands again.
